differences.what: the 1874 rear range: brick, as tall as the main block's wall head, behind the main block's north half, its south face long and its east face short
differences.how: T-3240: a K01 rear wing 17.7 x 6.8 m to a 10.0 m wall head; its south-east corner renders on the photograph's (x 545), its east face's north end on its edge

differences.what: round-headed lights on the range's south and east faces, two a storey on the east face
differences.how: T-3240: the wing's round heads, the east face's two a storey rendering over the photograph's

differences.what: the corbelled oriel on the range's south face at the upper storey
differences.how: T-3242: a K08 canted oriel on the range's south face (range_oriel), its front rendering over the photograph's (x 439-487), its floor at the range's second floor on seven corbel courses down to about 4.9 m (the photograph's brackets reach about 4.6 m), a pair of round-headed lights in its front and a square-headed one in each cheek; the wall under it now stands (a wing no longer cuts it from grade under an oriel). Its carved brackets and cresting are drawn as plain corbel courses and a low hip

differences.what: the range's heavy bracketed cornice and the low roof over it
differences.how: T-3257: the main block's own cornice (K10's bracketed timber, paired at 1.6 m) carried round the range's three walls under its deck's soffit (rear_wings[].roof.cornice): its pairs render along the photograph's south and east faces under the eave, and the line runs level into the main block's cornice where the photograph's does (x 305-320). The low roof over it is not seen from the lawn, so the range keeps its tin deck behind the fascia

differences.what: the high stone basement exposed at the range's east end over the falling lawn
differences.how: the review renders on one flat plane (the camera's solve); the ground's fall to the lake is the terrain's, not the house's

differences.what: the two-level columned veranda with its balustrades and the steps down to the lawn, against the main block's rear wall
differences.how: T-3242: k01_rear_veranda's two decks (1.85 and 5.2 m) on five stations of paired posts, the spindle frieze under the upper deck and a balustrade round both, render over the photograph's between the range and the main block's corner; the flight comes down off the lower deck's north bay where the photograph's does (its foot at about x 340)

differences.what: the main block's railed deck over its roof, seen above the rear
differences.how: T-3241: the deck's rail (k01_hip_deck) stands over the hip where the photograph shows it, above the rear wall's cornice

differences.what: the main block's south end at the left of the picture, a two-storey bay on its south face
differences.how: T-3241: the lower south range now stands at the picture's left edge where the photograph's low block does; the rear copy (675 px) reads the mass over it as a two-storey bay, while the front photograph shows the flank over the range plain, its single light and its pair: two pictures that disagree, so the front's reading is followed

differences.what: the veranda's south end: the photograph's runs on past where the model's main block turns its corner, about 40 px further left (x 137 against 179)
differences.how: T-3257: two camera fits disagree about the main block's width: the front camera renders both of its street corners on the photograph's (the 1911 sheet's 14.7 m, chicagology_front: massing), this one reads its rear wall about 2 m wider. The veranda stands to the block's corner, so it follows the block the front fit holds

differences.what: the range's south face: the photograph's upper storey has one light west of the oriel (x 413), its lower two (x 390 and 425)
differences.how: T-3257: the face lists its lights by storey (rear_wings[].windows_by_storey): the lower storey's three at s 2.6, 7.2 and 10.0, the upper storey's at s 2.6 and 9.0, rendering on the photograph's x 413, and none over 7.2

differences.what: the veranda's turned posts and balusters and the brackets at its posts' heads
differences.how: T-3242 draws them square at the photograph's sizes: at this picture's scale (a post is about 2 px) a visitor reads the paired posts, the spindle band and the rails, which stand where the photograph's do

differences.what: the main block's south flank lights at the left of the picture, under their light hoods
differences.how: T-3255: the flank's lights now carry the eared and crested hoods the front photograph shows (eared_round_heads); at this distance they read as the photograph's pale heads. Nothing else in this view moved.

differences.what: the range's cornice at its near (south-east) corner: about 20 px higher in the photograph than in the render (the fit reads its bed at about 10.8 m over grade, against the main block's 10.0 m wall head built)
differences.how: T-3257: the photograph shows the range's cornice running level into the main block's, and there (x 305-320) the render's lies on the photograph's; the front camera holds the main block's cornice at its 10.0 m wall head. One level cornice cannot stand at both readings, so the gap is the fit's (its eye solved under the house's grade on a falling lawn), two readings disagreeing

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
